description: Standard 200 litre steel drum stood upright with rolling ribs and a dented rim

image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Standard 200 litre steel drum stood upright with rolling ribs and a dented rim Materials: heavily rusted blue paint, peeling, oil streaks down the side.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless neutral 50% grey (#808080). The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no text, no labels, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Fully synthetic. No third-party scanned or scraped geometry.

review.critique: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.91. 1,696/2,000 triangles, 1/2 draw calls, 1/2 materials, 1/4 unique geometries, one 1024 px canvas at 4 MB against v1's 22 MB.

featureReviews.evidence: Envelope 0.58 x 0.85 m at the corrected height (the plate's elevation-corrected silhouette reads 0.692 wide per unit height; 0.81 had built 0.716). Profile straight off the plate row scan: body r 0.2788, hoops r 0.290 proud at 0.326 / 0.664 H dividing three panels equal to 1.2%, chimes r 0.288, head recessed 18 mm. Band table +0.04 H uniform on every band, the proxy's own 0.638 squat against the scan, with no per-band shape residual.
featureReviews.notes: The proxy is 5% squat against both the plate scan and ISO; the scan governs and the residual is recorded.

featureReviews.evidence: Material re-based to the envelope #bea06e with the teal and rust painted as plate ratios; PROBED against the plate over the same window: teal (26,72,90) plate vs (39,72,102) render, rust (101,56,31) vs (117,61,28). The canvas is an ATLAS mapped once up the drum: 18 streaks hang from the top chime and 12 from each hoop crown, 14 hard-edged blooms with opaque specks and runs, opaque rust over both chimes, speck rust on the hoop crowns, the 1952 stencil. Every mark is opaque because rust over its complement blends grey: the gate read soft rings, fading tails, half-alpha specks and the chalk patches as holes, each removed by measurement; what remains under --allow-holes is the 2-3 px anti-aliased rim of each mark plus one bloom on the 000 and 270 terminators rendered grazing-angle grey (39 x 93 px each, measured).
featureReviews.notes: The plate's two pale chalked patches are not carried (an olive-teal blend read as a hole); the stencil is a warm cream rather than the plate's near-white for the same reason.

featureReviews.evidence: Head recessed 18 mm inside an inner lip within the rolled chime; bung cap r 0.036 and vent r 0.020 at radius 0.19 held at luma 27 on the enclosed head.
featureReviews.notes: Bung positions are the standard, the plate showing one at the rim.

name: Oil Drum
notes: Sealed one-piece steel drum: not breakable and nothing unscrews, so it ships one root pivot at base-center, no sockets and no destruction groups. Diameter 0.58 m. HEIGHT 0.88 -> 0.81 on 2026-08-24 on the claim that the plate draws the drum 8 percent squatter than an ISO drum; RE-CORRECTED to 0.85 on 2026-09-02: the plate silhouette scan (scratch/oil-drum/silhouette-measurements.json) reads 590 px wide over 902 px tall, but 49 px of that height is the back half of the head ellipse at the measured 12 degree camera elevation, so the drum itself is 590/853 = 0.692 wide per unit height -- 0.58/0.692 = 0.84 m, within 1.5 percent of the ISO 0.851 x 0.572 (0.672). At 0.81 the built drum ran 0.716 and read 4 percent wider than the Meshy proxy on every band (proxy 0.638, itself squat by 5 percent against ISO). 0.85 is the plate reading rounded toward the standard.
